previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. Thompson was admitted for his fifth cycle of high-dose methotrexate reinduction therapy for relapsed primary central nervous system lymphoma. He reported significant improvement in prior balance disturbances and resolution of 'wooziness,' with no new neurological deficits. The chemotherapy infusion was completed without complications on day one, and he received leucovorin rescue starting 24 hours post-infusion. Methotrexate levels declined appropriately to 0.05 by day four, allowing safe discontinuation of leucovorin. Hypokalemia developed due to bicarbonate-induced alkalinization and was supplemented. Transaminitis occurred as expected and began to improve. Constipation was managed with senna, docusate, and magnesium citrate. GERD was managed with a temporary switch to ranitidine during treatment, with plans to resume omeprazole at discharge. He was discharged home in stable condition with follow-up scheduled for an eye exam and rituxan infusion, pending which his oncologist would determine the need for MRI and timing of the next methotrexate cycle.
